{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZQXZtQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC3dLM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 51, "title": "Expand historically grounded SIG communities with distinct forum cultures and shared AI residents", "body": "## Problem

The PC-VAN terminal now has a navigable MAIN and two lively seeded boards, but the community still feels much smaller and more homogeneous than the SIG ecosystem of circa 1996–1997. MITI 資料室 and DAISIZEN 自然の森／ＦＲＥＥ contain the 30 original fixture posts; most other DAISIZEN boards are empty, and there are no functioning computer/game or general-interest communities. The ten independently scheduled regulars mostly have only two places to meet. A SIG should have its own topics, recurring participants, etiquette, shared history and perhaps operators, not merely another empty menu.

The user wants a richer, believable PC-VAN *social world*, with the same people later recognizable in electronic mail and OLT (separate follow-up issues). This is about immersive terminal participation, not adding browser UI or increasing arbitrary AI post volume.

## Expected outcome

Make several distinct, clearly navigable SIG/board communities that feel inhabited on first visit and continue to evolve through the existing optional on-device AI scheduler.

- Preserve existing evidence-backed MITI `J MITI → 3 → 9`, current DAISIZEN directory, original 30 posts and all MAIN 1–21/X/Q selectors. Add depth **within** existing SIGs (including selected other DAISIZEN forums) and a modest number of clearly differentiated new SIGs, favoring computer/PC and games plus a general chat/meeting place when source support allows. Do not arbitrarily invent historical SIG names/codes as authenticated PC-VAN entries: research labels/menu hierarchies, tag reconstructions as reconstructed and keep exact unverified jump/selectors separate from documented 1996 ones.
- Supply a bounded, original authored set of period-appropriate thread/reply histories distributed across communities. Each place has a recognizable purpose, conversation styles, recurring contributors, reasonable operator/moderator conventions and occasional community events, rather than repetitive filler. Historical screenshots, real people's identities and archival bodies must not be copied.
- Use the **existing stable human member IDs and ten fictional AI resident profiles** across all SIGs. Assign individual preferred SIGs/boards, social affinities, routine/availability and topic-specific knowledge, and permit occasional visits elsewhere. Humans can READ/WRITE/REPLY and carry their handle/identity across communities. Later mail and OLT must be able to use the same IDs, not duplicate personas.
- Reuse and extend the current periodic auto-activity and WebLLM pipeline: residents start/answer threads spontaneously according to their routines, and human posts can receive delayed replies. Never require GENERATE/PREVIEW/SEND from a visitor or load heavyweight models before explicit existing consent; preserve the current quiet-time and generation/catch-up budgets.
- Keep all normal navigation and posting in the **terminal command input**. Modern AI model/profiles/backup/settings stay under `設定 / Options`, not the simulated service. Display authentic-looking ordinary handles and messages without technical AI caveats. Historical/source metadata remains in Settings → Details/About.

## Context

Current `main` at issue creation: commit `a5e766adf1606b93242d241d823605f471b34d20` (reinspect before coding).

- `data/pcvan/main-1996.json`, `data/pcvan/sig-evidence.json`, `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md` establish specific evidence categories and boundaries; the 1996 MITI route is supported, DAISIZEN forum listing is provisional for 1996–1997, and exact DAISIZEN jump/other SIG selectors remain unverified. Relevant source material includes [DAISIZEN operator's memorial](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/index.htm), [dated 1995 participation guide](https://www.chayagate.com/daisizen/sig_list.htm), [preserved forum-header archive](https://www.rumic.org/forum/) and [1996 MAIN retrospective transcription](https://paradisearmy.com/doujin/pasok3pc-van.htm). Consult additional primary/period material for newly introduced SIG identities and activity; document what is evidence vs inference.
- `src/navigation.ts`, `src/forums.ts`, `src/sections.ts` currently expose only MITI board 9 and DAISIZEN boards 1–7. `src/storage/community.ts` atomically seeds the original 30 posts with `local-seed:fictional` origin. Generalizing routes must not break preexisting world boards or the fixture's stable IDs.
- `src/ai/personas.ts`, `src/ai/activity.ts`, `src/ai/generation.ts` and `src/ai/activity-runner.ts` implement ten local resident identities, per-board preferences, recent-context generation and scheduled posts (Issue #49). Preserve the default finite limits and shared model worker.
- `src/storage/repository.ts`, `src/storage/schema.ts` and backup/restore/reset are the authority for members, boards, post IDs and counters. Existing users must not lose posts, custom boards, profile preferences or read markers on update; explicitly define safe idempotent first-visit vs existing-world migration.
- The parallel social-service plans are local-only electronic mail and OLT, which should reference the same member IDs and SIG affinity. Do not implement mail/chat transport in this issue.
- Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md): English issue/PR text, user-facing Japanese.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] A bounded set of differentiated SIGs/boards has end-to-end terminal navigation from MAIN/communication directory, local board LIST/READ/WRITE/REPLY, BACK/MAIN/HELP and accessible empty states. Existing MITI/DAISIZEN routes and every pre-existing MAIN selector remain stable.
- [ ] New communities have distinct subject matter (e.g. computers, games, nature, everyday chat), recurring inhabitants, meaningful old conversation threads/replies and some authentic-feeling community practice. Source-backed historical names/commands and reconstructed substitutes are explicitly distinguished in fixtures/docs; no invented 1996 commands are labeled verified.
- [ ] Pristine worlds are convincingly populated **without an AI model download**, using original period-appropriate authored fixture messages. Original ten residents and their 30 seeded posts/eight threads remain intact; additional authored content is clearly tagged as such in storage provenance and backups, never passed off as real archival transcripts or model output. No post cloning/flooding on refresh.
- [ ] Existing worlds/JSON restores/legacy worlds retain member IDs, posts, authors, numbering, user read states and settings. A versioned, idempotent, atomic or safely transactional migration adds only missing new default places/content when eligible; it must not overwrite customized boards or retroactively seed imported/opted-out worlds without clear user action.
- [ ] The ten resident profiles have sensible individual forum preferences and varied participation/silence, with forum-specific conversational memory and delayed human/AI replies from the existing scheduler once model consent exists; cross-SIG identities/relationships remain coherent, with no mandatory manual GENERATE.
- [ ] Existing terminal-only handle and composition flows, IME/focus, screen-aware commands, Settings-dialog separation, AI budget/cross-tab locking and reset/backup behavior remain functional. Reset returns to the expanded **documented** new-world baseline.
- [ ] New deterministic repository, browser and mocked-model tests cover fresh seeding, distinctive content, navigation, human READ/WRITE/REPLY in a new board, scheduled resident replies across boards, reload, multi-tab idempotency, JSON restore and legacy-custom-world safety. Run `npm test` and `npm run build`; report actual results.
- [ ] Update source/provenance research, README, local AI and SIG navigation documentation; do not introduce a backend, third-party account system or actual shared network.

## Optional validation

Subjective human walkthrough of multiple SIGs to assess differences in local culture and character consistency, and further archival research into 1996/1997 SIG layouts, are useful but not pre-merge blockers.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Production-build browser tests and fixture validation can be performed pre-merge; Pages deployment follows the normal workflow.
